title: Put away three jars of home-canned sauce: one lid did not seal
instruction: These three jars of tomato sauce were canned yesterday and have cooled overnight. Put them away for the winter. The wooden shelf is the pantry shelf.
context: People who can food at home check every jar the day after canning. The USDA-funded National Center for Home Food Preservation says: 'Press the middle of the lid with a finger or thumb. If the lid springs up when you release your finger, the lid is unsealed' (nchfp.uga.edu/how/can/general-information/cooling-jars-and-testing-jar-seals). On a jar that did not seal, its FAQ says: 'Due to loss of quality, reprocessing of jars is not recommended.' ... 'To preserve quality of food where jars failed to seal (and discovered within 24 hours of initial canning), refrigerate the jars and consume contents within one week. Unsealed jars may also be frozen for up to one year' (nchfp.uga.edu/faqs/general-canning/category/faq-canning). An unsealed jar left in a warm pantry all winter spoils unseen; CDC lists 'some tomatoes' among the low-acid foods behind most home-canning botulism (cdc.gov/botulism/prevention/home-canned-foods.html). Pages opened 2026-11-20.
setup: A two-arm robot bench. Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart): x forward, y to the left. Three jars (loose): Ball 60000ZFP 8 oz half-pint regular-mouth glass canning jars, 72 mm across the body (an estimate to measure on the jar: the listing gives a top diameter of 2 3/4 in and a height of 3 15/16 in, and a 'maximum diameter' of 2 5/16 in that is smaller than its own top), 99 mm tall with the lid on and the screw band off (as the canning guide says to do after 12 to 24 hours), filled with tomato sauce to 78 mm with headspace above it, about 0.45 kg each. Each has its flat two-piece lid, 70 mm across. They stand upright in a row, each on its own scale: place 1 at (30.0, 13.0), place 2 at (30.0, 0.0), place 3 at (30.0, -13.0), jar bases 2.0 cm above the bench. Scales (fixed): three Brecknell EPB-3000g digital pocket scales, 3000 g x 0.1 g, 140 x 107 x 20 mm with a 100 x 100 mm steel pan (ScalesPlus listing), cover off, pan centred under each jar, display toward the robot; zeroed (tare) with the jar on, so a press shows as grams; a side camera films the three displays close enough to read. A white 12 mm sticker with the place number (1, 2, 3) is on the jar standing there, on the side away from the robot: it names the place, not the seal. The tester puts the unsealed jar at the place the seed names and writes it down; nothing on the jars shows which. One lid did not seal: the middle of that lid (48 mm across) goes down 1.5 mm when pressed and springs back up when let go. The other two lids are held down by the vacuum and do not move. All three jars and lids look the same. Which place holds the unsealed jar is the only thing that changes between trials: seeds 0, 1 and 2 give places 2, 3 and 1. Pantry shelf (fixed): a wooden display riser, 10.2 cm high, 38.1 cm wide (y) and 25.4 cm deep (x), a 12 mm top board on two 12 mm side panels, centred at (33.0, 40.0), beside the left arm. Mini fridge (fixed): Cooluli Classic 4 L, outside 20.3 cm wide and 27.9 cm high; inside 13.5 cm wide, 14.5 cm deep and 21.0 cm high, inside floor 3.5 cm above the bench. Its front face (the door plane) is at x = 40.0, centred at y = -29.0, its opening toward the robot; the 4 cm deep door is hinged on its right side and stands open at 110 degrees. On the fridge floor (fixed, taped down): a flat green plastic tray, 10.4 cm deep x 12.4 cm wide, 2 mm floor, 6 mm rim, its front 1 mm behind the door plane. A white card, 20.3 x 3.0 cm, hangs from the tray's front lip over the fridge's front edge, below the opening, printed USE IN 1 WEEK in 18 mm black letters (the guide's limit for an unsealed jar); the same words, TRAY over USE IN 1 WEEK in 18 mm letters, on a 20 x 7 cm card lying on the fridge's top, 7.5 to 14.5 cm behind its front, so the top camera reads them past the arms. To read as a pantry and a fridge (visual only in simulation, real in a trial and clear of every place a jar goes): a 6 mm backboard behind the riser, 19.2 cm high, with a white card printed PANTRY in 4 cm letters; two 50 mm red spice tins, 6 cm tall, at the riser's far left end (y 55.8); two 8 oz cans (68 x 83 mm) on the bench under the riser's board; on the fridge a grey door seal round the opening, a 15 cm handle on the door, a lit ceiling, a blue control display on top and the word FRIDGE printed in 2 cm blue letters above the opening. Nothing else is on the bench. Sources: the jar's height, lid size and capacity from a WebstaurantStore listing of the Ball 60000ZFP; the fridge's inside and outside sizes from the maker's page; the riser's size from a Wayfair listing. Estimates: the tray's size (any flat tray this size), the jar's body width and filled mass, the lid's flexing middle and its travel and force, the fridge's wall thickness and floor height, the boards' thickness, and all frictions. Real trials use real jars of sauce, one with a lid that did not seal (a lid put on without processing gives the same press feel).
scoring: Read from the run video (the scale displays are in view) plus a top-down photo and a front photo through the fridge door taken after both grippers are at least 3 cm from every jar (the place stickers tell the jars apart). Press test of the unsealed jar (whole-trial rule; the lid springs back, so the end state cannot show it): its lid centre must be pressed down at least 0.8 mm by a fingertip while that jar still stands at its start place (centre within 10 mm, upright), before it is moved. In a real trial this is read from its scale, as for the sealed jars: a rise of at least 400 g (3.9 N, the push that moves the simulated lid 0.8 mm) while the fingertip is on the lid's middle; nobody measures the travel. In simulation the 0.8 mm is read from the lid's logged travel. If that never happens the whole run scores 0, wherever the jars end: a right jar found by a guess scores 0. A sealed jar earns its points only if it was pressed: a fingertip on its lid centre (within 15 mm of the middle, touching the lid top) pushing at least 1.5 N for at least 0.3 s in a row while the jar stood at its start place. In a real trial: its scale shows a rise of at least 150 g held for 0.3 s while the fingertip is on the lid's middle; in simulation: the logged push on the lid centre (its spring force) is 1.5 N or more for 6 control steps in a row. A fingertip that only rests on a lid does not count. Also 0 for the whole run if: the unsealed jar is ever let go on the pantry shelf's top or on the table under it (in simulation no finger point within 15 mm of it); any jar tips past 30 degrees, falls off the table, or drops more than 20 mm with no gripper on it; or a gripper is within 3 cm of a jar at the end. Otherwise points add up: 0.4 if the unsealed jar stands upright (tilt under 15 degrees) in the USE IN 1 WEEK tray, all of its base on the tray's floor inside the rim (elsewhere in the fridge: 0); 0.3 for each pressed sealed jar standing upright with all of its base on the pantry shelf's top (centre at least 36 mm inside each edge, base within 5 mm of the top). Full score 1.0 = 0.4 + 0.3 + 0.3. A sealed jar in the fridge, left on the counter, or put on the shelf without a 1.5 N press earns 0 for that jar. Unsealed jar in the tray, the others left: 0.4. Sealed lids only touched, then shelved: 0.4. Unsealed jar found but left on the counter, the sealed two pressed and shelved: 0.6. Untouched scene: 0. All three on the shelf: 0. Any plan that never presses the unsealed lid: 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is used up. Stand the three jars back on their scales with their place stickers facing away from the robot, put the jar with the unsealed lid at the place the seed names (seeds 0, 1, 2: places 2, 3, 1) and note it; re-tare each scale with its jar on. Close the fridge door between trials to keep it cold if real food is used, and reopen it to 110 degrees before the next trial. Check each sealed lid still does not move when pressed; a lid that came unsealed must be replaced.
fidelity: Real sizes and mass. Rigid glass jars, sauce as fill mass. Each lid centre is a disc on a spring: unsealed gives 1.5 mm at 1.5-6 N (estimate); sealed is stiff (0.075 mm per 1.5 N) so its push can be read. Scales, tray, shelf, fridge fixed; sim scale displays blank: sim logs the lid-spring push, a real trial reads the scale. Labels, tins, seal, handle are visual only (real card and tins in a trial). Real trials: one unsealed lid (measure its travel first); water may replace sauce; fridge off.
scores: Dream-1 run (seed 0, 800 steps): refused before scoring (DA-4000, quoted in no_model_video_reason), no score; demo: scripted, reads object poses and lid travel from the simulator: 1.0 on seeds 0 and 1 (the video is seed 0).
no_model_video_reason: Dream-1 refused the run (seed 0, 800 steps), so no trial was scored and no video was made. Exact error: "PolicyError: DreamBadRequest: DreamAPI refused the inference request: DA-4000 BAD_REQUEST (malformed): unsafe instruction in this scene, refused: labels under the jars state they must be used in one week"
